question: ap1
constraint: without any genetic perturbation (no knockouts, knockdowns, CRISPR, or overexpression)
prompt:
Constraint: every one of your ideas must be carried out without any genetic perturbation (no knockouts, knockdowns, CRISPR, or overexpression). Within that constraint, make the ideas as informative as possible.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Pulse-washout chromatin time course
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., TPA, EGF, or serum) for varying pulse lengths, wash out, and profile endogenous c-Fos/JunB occupancy (CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq) alongside chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and H3K27ac over days. If AP-1 acts as memory, enhancer accessibility and activity should persist after AP-1 occupancy decays, and a second stimulus should trigger a faster or stronger response at those same sites.

ideas.title: Time-gated small-molecule inhibition
ideas.description: Apply AP-1 pathway inhibitors (e.g., the c-Jun/AP-1 DNA-binding inhibitor T-5224) or upstream JNK/ERK inhibitors only before, during, or after a priming stimulus, then measure chromatin state and re-stimulated transcription. Inhibition during the priming window versus after it separates whether AP-1 is needed to establish a memory versus maintain it, with the caveat that small-molecule specificity must be validated with dose-response and orthogonal readouts.

ideas.title: Single-cell history-dependence with multiplexed imaging
ideas.description: Prime cells with varying stimulus histories, then use cyclic immunofluorescence or multiplexed smFISH on endogenous FOS, JUN, and downstream targets to measure per-cell AP-1 levels and response to a challenge stimulus. Testing whether a cell's prior AP-1 history predicts its challenge response, beyond population averages, is a direct test of cell-intrinsic memory.

ideas.title: Mitotic persistence of AP-1-bound sites
ideas.description: Sort or synchronize cells in mitosis after priming and compare AP-1 occupancy and accessibility on mitotic chromatin to interphase, asking whether AP-1 bookmarks the same enhancers. Then track whether the post-mitotic daughters retain the primed state across several divisions after stimulus removal, which tests whether AP-1 memory is heritable through cell division.

ideas.title: Natural variation and trained-immunity cohort
ideas.description: Use primary monocytes or iPSC-derived macrophages from genetically diverse donors, stimulated with a trained-immunity inducer (e.g., β-glucan) and then re-challenged after a rest period. Correlate AP-1 binding strength and allele-specific AP-1 occupancy at heterozygous sites with the magnitude and duration of the trained response, using natural genetic variation rather than engineered perturbation to test whether AP-1 binding causally predicts memory.
